question: Should OpenClaw permanently adopt one globally unique two-part coverage ID per taxonomy feature and make the 11-category `smoke-ci` profile the authoritative scope for the fixed 12-scenario plan?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent and prior review found no discrete code defect, but the chosen identifier vocabulary and smoke-profile eligibility rules determine long-lived QA reporting semantics that tests cannot choose on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Adopt the strict contract
options.body: Approve one exact two-part ID per feature and the narrowed smoke profile after exact-head CI is green.

options.title: Keep broader profile semantics
options.body: Retain the existing broader `smoke-ci` category selection and request a narrower uniqueness-only refactor.

options.title: Pause for QA design review
options.body: Hold the PR until a QA owner documents the desired relationship between fixed smoke scenarios, categories, and maturity reporting.

recommendation.title: Adopt the strict contract
recommendation.body: Approve one exact two-part ID per feature and the narrowed smoke profile after exact-head CI is green.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the reconciliation evidence and are the available context's direct owner of the proposed taxonomy and smoke-profile model.
